```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# get park data
ballparks_stadium_data <- read_csv("data/ballparks_stadium_data_2022.csv")
head(ballparks_stadium_data)
```

```{r}
# get downloaded hitter stats
`2022HitterStats` <- read_csv("data/2022HitterStats.csv")
head(`2022HitterStats`)
```


```{r}
Player_team_info <- mlb_stats(stat_type = 'season', stat_group = 'hitting', season = 2022) |>
  select(player_id, team_name, league_name)
head(Player_team_info)


Full_22_Hitter_stats <- `2022HitterStats` |>
  left_join(Player_team_info, join_by(player_id))
head(Full_22_Hitter_stats)


```
```{r}
# elevation density plot
ggplot(ballparks_stadium_data, aes(x = elevation)) +
  geom_density() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of MLB Park Elevations", x = "Elevation (feet)")
```

```{r}
#|fig-alt: "Ridgeline plot showing the distribution of On-Base Percentage across different MLB teams for the 2022 season. Each team's density curve illustrates the spread of player OBP values, with color differentiation enhancing team distinction. Denser areas indicate where players' on-base percentages are more concentrated within a team"

ggplot(Full_22_Hitter_stats, aes(x = on_base_percent, y = reorder(team_name, on_base_percent), fill = team_name)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    scale = 2.5, 
    alpha = 0.9, 
    size = 0.3, 
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9) +  # broader color range
  labs(
    x = "On-Base Percentage",
    y = "Team Name",
    title = "Distribution of On-Base Percentage by Team (2022 Season)",
    subtitle = "Ridgeline plot showing variability across teams",
    caption = "Source: 2022 MLB Hitter Stats"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "italic"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)  # make team names smaller to avoid overlapping
  )
```

```{r}

# Expected vs Observed slugging percentage by teams in national league west
ggplot(National_League_West_22, aes(x = xslg, y = slg_percent, color = team_name)) +
  geom_point()  +
    geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Expected SLG", y = "Observed SLG", color = "Team Name",
       title = "Observed vs. Expected SLG by Hitter (colored by Park) in National League West teams") +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
# Actual vs Expected Batting Average
ggplot(joined_stadium_data, aes(x = xba, y = batting_avg, color = league_name)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs. Expected Batting Average",
    x = "Expected BA (xba)",
    y = "Observed BA (batting_avg)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#Park Effects vs. Hard-Hit % 
ggplot(joined_stadium_data, aes(x = hr_park_effects, y = hard_hit_percent, color = ballpark)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "HR Park Effects vs. Hard-Hit %",
    x = "HR Park Effects (100 = avg)",
    y = "Hard-Hit %"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#Extra Distance → Home Runs
# If you haven't already installed showtext, do it first
# install.packages("showtext")

library(showtext)

# Add custom font (e.g., Press Start 2P)
font_add_google("Press Start 2P", "baseball_font")
showtext_auto()

joined_stadium_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(extra_distance), !is.na(home_run)) %>%
  group_by(ballpark) %>%
  filter(n() > 0) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = extra_distance, y = home_run, color = ballpark)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Extra Distance and Home Runs",
    caption = "Source: Baseball Savant 2022",
    x = "Extra Distance (in Yards)",
    y = "Total Number of Home Runs",
    color = "Ballpark"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 9, family = "baseball_font"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8, family = "baseball_font"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", family = "baseball_font"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, family = "baseball_font")
  )


```

```{r}
# Field Dimensions: Left vs. Right (size = park factor)
ggplot(joined_stadium_data, aes(x = left_field, y = right_field, size = hr_park_effects)) +

  labs(

    x = "Left Field Distance (yd)",
    y = "Right Field Distance (yd)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```



```{r}
# Vis of woba vs xwoba vs park effect

library(mlbplotR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

# Load MLB team logos and other info
teams_colors_logos <- mlbplotR::load_mlb_teams() |> 
  dplyr::filter(!team_abbr %in% c("AL", "NL", "MLB"))

# Merge the logos with your data
player_and_park_stats_with_logos <- player_and_park_stats |>
  dplyr::left_join(teams_colors_logos, by = c("team_name" = "team_name"))

# Filter for specific teams (example teams)
filtered_data <- player_and_park_stats_with_logos |>
  filter(team_name %in% c("Baltimore Orioles", "Houston Astros", "Los Angeles Dodgers", 
                          "New York Mets", "New York Yankees", "Seattle Mariners", 
                          "Toronto Blue Jays", "San Diego Padres"))

# Normalize the 'hr_park_effects' column for logo size scaling (to keep sizes reasonable)
filtered_data$logo_size <- scales::rescale(filtered_data$hr_park_effects, to = c(0.1, 0.2))  # Adjusted scaling

# Adjust logo size by applying a scaling factor to make all logos smaller overall
scaling_factor <- 0.3  # New factor for overall smaller logos

# Create the plot with trend line, logos, and size variation
ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = woba, y = xwoba)) +
  mlbplotR::geom_mlb_logos(aes(team_abbr = team_abbr), 
                           width = scaling_factor * filtered_data$logo_size, 
                           alpha = 0.8) +  # Adjust logo size by the scaling factor
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Park Effects Size", range = c(1, 6), guide = guide_legend(title = "Park Effects")) +  # Size legend
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs. Expected wOBA by MLB Team",
    x = "wOBA",
    y = "xwOBA",
    caption = "Source: Baseball Savant 2022"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold", family = "baseball_font"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", family = "baseball_font"),
    legend.position = "right",  # Place legend on the right
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.key.size = unit(1, "cm")  # Adjust legend size
  ) +
  # Add trend line using geom_abline (with slope = 1 and intercept = 0)
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "black", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) 



```

```{r}
player_and_park_stats |>
  filter(team_name %in% c("Baltimore Orioles", "Seattle Mariners", "Los Angeles Dodgers")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = team_name, size = hr_park_effects)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +  # Adjust alpha for better visibility
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "black", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +  # Add trend line (y = x line)
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs Expected wOBA for Selected MLB Teams",
    x = "wOBA",
    y = "xwOBA",
    caption = "Source: Baseball Savant 2022",
    color = "Team",
    size = "Park Factor"
  
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Baltimore Orioles" = "orange", 
                                "Seattle Mariners" = "green", 
                                "Los Angeles Dodgers" = "red")) +  # Set team-specific colors
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Park Effect Size", range = c(3, 8)) +  # Adjust point sizes based on park effect, with a more readable range
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, face = "bold", family = "baseball_font"),  # Smaller title size
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8, "baseball_font"),  # Smaller axis title size
    legend.position = "right",  # Place legend on the right
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),  # Smaller legend title size
    legend.key.size = unit(1, "cm")  # Adjust legend size
  )

player_and_park_stats |>

  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Baltimore Orioles" = "orange", 
                                "Seattle Mariners" = "green", 
                                "Los Angeles Dodgers" = "red")) +  # Set team-specific colors
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Park Effect Size", range = c(3, 8)) +  # Adjust point sizes based on park effect, with a more readable range
```
